messages:
alex: Quick follow-up from the attention-kernels RFC — we need to decide whether to prototype a CUTLASS/CUDA attention path for 8-bit quant workloads or continue investing in Triton fused-attn. I want a short action list and owners.

pranav: My quick take: CUTLASS gives better throughput on Ampere/Turing for matmul-heavy flows, but Triton keeps fused kernels + easier dev iteration. Need numbers for A100 vs T4.

maria: Also consider maintenance: Triton = Python-first kernels -> faster push cycles. CUTLASS -> C++/CUDA templates, more build infra. Ops will care.

kevin: From runtime API side, if we add CUTLASS we should avoid explosion of config flags. Suggest runtime kernel_supplier: `triton|cutlass|auto` and a fallback_policy.

jen: Tests/CI: we'll need a GPU matrix for both kernel paths. Can't run CUTLASS on mac builders. Propose adding A100 and T4 runners to CI pool for these benches.

chao: License/third-party: CUTLASS is Apache2 but we should audit included examples + vendor code. Also ask infra about cross-compilation for our private deployment.

pranav: I'll prototype a minimal CUTLASS attention wrapper that supports KV-caching and int8 GEMM path. Plan: run bench against Triton fused-attn for these configs:
```
python bench/attn_bench.py --model gpt2 --quant 8 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --device a100
python bench/attn_bench.py --model gpt2 --quant 8 --batch 4 --seq 512 --device t4
```
Expect to compare p50 latency, p95, and tokens/sec.

kevin: Good. Also define runtime behavior when CUTLASS isn't available: `kernel_supplier: auto` should pick best based on device capability + model quantization. Fallback rules: prefer low-latency supplier but fallback to `triton` if kernel fails.

alex: Important: accuracy/regression risk with 8-bit kernels. Need a small eval harness that runs prompt-suite and checks generation diffs + perplexity. Maria, can your team own that?

maria: Yes. I'll add a regression job that runs our canonical prompt set on CPU float baseline and both kernel paths. Need to define acceptance thresholds (e.g., token-level edit distance < 0.5% or KL threshold).

jen: CI tasks: add a `cutlass` label to bench jobs, and a nightly perf job that posts to #eng-releases with a summary. I can wire alerts if p50 increases > 10%.

pranav: Implementation notes: CUTLASS path will expose a small C API wrapper + Python binding. We'll keep the runtime APi unchanged: just implement a KernelBackend interface. Minimal patch: ~3 files (wrapper, registry, build rules).

kevin: I'll draft an RFC amendment describing the KernelBackend interface + selection heuristics. Will include a state machine for rollouts: canary -> A/B -> full. Mention canary size and metrics.

chao: I'll do the legal/license check and confirm we can ship CUTLASS examples in our distro. Also will check NVIDIA compatibility matrix for older drivers.

ci-bot: nightly/bench-a100: queued -> estimated 45m. Attached run template: `bench/attn_bench.py --seq 1024 --batch 8`

alex: Action items (short):
- pranav: prototype CUTLASS wrapper + microbench (due +3 weeks)
- kevin: RFC amendment + selection API (due +1 week)
- maria: regression harness + acceptance thresholds (due +2 weeks)
- jen: CI GPUs + nightly bench + alerts (due +2 weeks)
- chao: license/compat audit (due +1 week)
- ops/sre: define canary rollout config (see @sre-bot)

sre-bot: FYI: canary guidance: start at 2% traffic, monitor latency, error-rate, and token-drop. Auto-rollback if error-rate > 0.5% or p95 latency regresses > 20%.

maria: For the acceptance thresholds: propose token-level edit distance < 0.3% and KL < 0.01 on sample corpus. Will iterate if teams object.

pranav: One more perf detail: CUTLASS wins when sequence length is short/medium and quant GEMM dominates. For long seq we might want Triton's fused-attn because of better kernel fusion and KV-cache reuse. Will capture in heuristics.

kevin: We'll need telemetry hooks: kernel_supplier chosen, kernel_version, fallback_count, per-request latency breakdown. Add these to the tracing/span attributes.

jen: I'll add win/lose flags to bench outputs and push a small dashboard: tokens/sec vs mem/latency.

alex: OK. If no objections, we'll proceed with these owners. We'll reconvene in 1 week for RFC draft and initial infra changes. Thanks. :thumbsup:

pranav: 👍 starting prototype today.

chao: noted, will update license doc by EOW.

kevin: RFC PR incoming tomorrow.

jen: I'll open CI tickets and link them here.
